scope: Round 14. SRS.txt 'System - API for RAG - chatbox': write & retrieve data APIs, expected error handling, auth & authz on all routes, prompt ejection blocking middleware, global error handler, soft delete.

source_requirements.text: Role description: You're my code-agent, i'm gonna create a sites for system auction, read all Requirements below, then write me a feature-list.json file, with e2e function, unit and intergration tests write to e2e folder. System - API for RAG - chatbox. description and priority: Priority high. write me all api for write, retrieve datas for RAG chatbox system. api error should return expected error. Req-1: all routes have both authenticated and authorized. Req-2: Sercurity by block prompt ejection - middleware. Req-3: Api error handle global - catch all unexpected errors

readings_to_confirm: Req-1: all routes have both authenticated (valid token via cookie or Authorization header) and authorized (role checks: customer/staff/admin for chat & retrieve; staff/admin for docs management). 401 for unauthenticated, 403 for unauthorized.
Req-2: security middleware blocks prompt ejection/injection attempts across request bodies and queries before processing, returning HTTP 400 with expected JSON error.
Req-3: global error handler catches all unexpected exceptions and standard HTTP errors (400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 413, 429, 500) and returns structured JSON { 'error': '<message>' }.

Write and retrieve APIs: POST /api/docs (write doc + auto-chunks + embeddings), GET /api/docs (retrieve list), GET /api/docs/<id> (retrieve doc & chunks), POST /api/rag/retrieve (retrieve relevant chunks for query), DELETE /api/docs/<id> (soft delete with deleted_at).
All delete operations are soft delete (setting deleted_at timestamp); deleted items are excluded from retrieval.
Tests: unit tests in be/rag/*_test.py, integration/e2e tests in e2e/rag-chat-api.spec.ts.

features.srs_ref: SRS Req-3: Api error handle global - catch all unexpected errors; api error should return expected error
features.title: Global API error handling middleware with structured JSON responses
features.user_visible_behavior: All unexpected exceptions and standard HTTP error codes (400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 413, 429, 500) return a consistent JSON response format `{'error': '<message>'}` without HTML tracebacks.
acceptance: Flask global error handlers registered for standard HTTP errors and generic Exception.
Responses have Content-Type application/json with JSON body containing `error` key.
404 returns `{'error': 'Not Found'}`.
405 returns `{'error': 'Method Not Allowed'}`.
Unhandled exceptions return HTTP 500 `{'error': 'Internal server error'}`.
Python unit tests verify global error handling across error statuses.

features.srs_ref: SRS Req-2: Sercurity by block prompt ejection - middleware
features.title: Security middleware blocking prompt ejection and injection attacks
features.user_visible_behavior: Requests containing prompt ejection or jailbreak patterns (e.g. 'ignore previous instructions', system prompt leaks, roleplay overrides) are intercepted and rejected with HTTP 400 and an expected error message.
acceptance: Middleware inspects incoming JSON request bodies and query parameters before route execution.
Identifies prompt ejection signatures (instruction bypass, system prompt exfiltration, roleplay jailbreaks).
Rejects matching requests immediately with HTTP 400 `{'error': 'Prompt injection detected'}`.
Legitimate requests pass through without alteration or blockage.
Python unit tests verify blocking of various injection payloads and pass-through of valid prompts.

features.srs_ref: SRS Req-1: all routes have both authenticated and authorized
features.title: Authentication and authorization enforcement on all RAG and Chat routes
features.user_visible_behavior: Every API route requires valid authentication (via cookie or Authorization Bearer header) and validates the user's role/permission before allowing access. Missing auth returns 401; insufficient role returns 403.
acceptance: Authentication helper supports both cookie `auction_token` and `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`.
POST /api/chat and POST /api/rag/retrieve require authenticated user (customer, staff, admin); unauthenticated receives 401.
POST /api/docs, GET /api/docs, GET /api/docs/<id>, DELETE /api/docs/<id> require staff or admin role; non-staff/admin receives 403.
Invalid, expired, or locked/disabled user tokens return 401 `{'error': 'Authentication required'}`.
Python unit tests verify 401 unauthenticated and 403 forbidden scenarios across all routes.

features.srs_ref: SRS: write me all api for write, retrieve datas for RAG chatbox system; All delete mean soft delete
features.title: Complete Write and Retrieve Data APIs for RAG System with Soft Delete
features.user_visible_behavior: Authorized users can write documents (auto-chunked and embedded before saving), retrieve document lists, retrieve single document details with chunks, retrieve relevant chunks for a search query, and soft-delete documents.
acceptance: POST /api/docs writes document, auto-chunked via `rag.chunk_text` and embedded before saving; returns HTTP 201.
GET /api/docs retrieves all active (non-soft-deleted) documents.
GET /api/docs/<int:doc_id> retrieves a single document with its metadata and chunk details; returns 404 if deleted or not found.
POST /api/rag/retrieve embeds the query and retrieves top matching chunks from active documents.
DELETE /api/docs/<int:doc_id> soft-deletes the document and its chunks by setting `deleted_at = now()`; returns 204.
Soft-deleted documents and chunks are excluded from retrieval and chat context.
Python unit/integration tests verify write, retrieve, search, and soft-delete operations.

Covers prompt injection blocking (middleware intercepts attack payloads).

Covers full lifecycle: write document -> chunk verification -> retrieve query -> soft delete -> verify excluded.
All test suites pass cleanly; change docs created in docs/changes/.
